# Enable SaaS Browsing

## Goal

Configure a fixed business website as a SaaS site so employees can enter it directly from the Sa2web user frontend and reuse a remote browser account that an administrator has already logged in to.

SaaS browsing is suitable when multiple people share the same business account. The administrator logs in to a site in the backend first. Authorized frontend users then access the site in an already logged-in state.

## Create a Site Category

Go to:

```text
Site Management > Site Category Management
```

Create categories by business area, such as foreign trade platforms, customer service systems, data analytics, and common systems, as shown in @fig-site-category.

![Sa2web site category management](/images/site-category.png){#fig-site-category}

## Add a SaaS Site

Go to:

```text
Site Management > Site List
```

When adding a site, as shown in @fig-add-site, fill in:

- Site name.
- Full `https://` URL.
- Category.
- Logo.
- Description.
- Status.
- Account category.

![Sa2web add SaaS site](/images/add-site.png){#fig-add-site}

After the site is added, it appears in the site list, as shown in @fig-site-list.

![Sa2web site list](/images/site-list.png){#fig-site-list}

## Create an Account Type and Browser Account

Go to:

```text
Site Management > Site Browser Account
```

Create a browser account for the target site. After saving, click the "![](/images/login.png){width=20px}" button in the list so the remote browser opens the target site and completes login, as shown in @fig-site-browser-account.

![Sa2web site browser account login](/images/site-browser-account.png){#fig-site-browser-account}

## Group Authorization

Authorize the following resources in the group:

- Users.
- SaaS sites.

Select the SaaS site in the group, as shown in @fig-group-privileges-site.

![Sa2web group authorization for SaaS sites](/images/group-privileges-site.png){#fig-group-privileges-site}

## User Access

Users log in at:

```text
https://<APP_DOMAIN>/app/login
```

On the user home page, as shown in @fig-user-access-saas, click the authorized site to enter the remote browser and access the SaaS site, as shown in @fig-user-access-saas-site.

![Sa2web user center](/images/user-access-saas.png){#fig-user-access-saas}

![Sa2web user access to a SaaS site](/images/user-access-saas-site.png){#fig-user-access-saas-site}

Because the administrator has already completed login in the backend, users enter the SaaS site in a logged-in state. The account name is automatically hidden according to configuration so frontend users do not see shared account information.

## Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] The user frontend can show the authorized site.
- [ ] Unauthorized users cannot see the site.
- [ ] Clicking the site opens the remote browser.
- [ ] The corresponding browser account remains logged in.
